claims.claim: History & Rollback's proposed flow pushes the rollback commit directly to the sync branch outside the commit server (T-27327's `git checkout / commit / push $sync_branch`). Once the signing feature in T-28239 is enabled and the target branch's SourceIntegrity policy requires verified signatures, that push lands unsigned and the git host rejects it. The Rollback button just shows a failed push with no signing-aware message and no retry path from the History and Rollback tab — the operator is stuck until someone manually finds and fixes the commit server's signing key config.

rfc-002's push-to-stage hydration mode has no freshness signal exposed to the user: T-26443 shows that when the sync source changes with auto-sync on, Argo CD immediately syncs whatever manifests already sit on the stage/sync branch path before the external promoter has moved fresh ones in. The Application shows an ordinary Synced/Healthy state throughout, so there is no stale/dirty indicator distinguishing 'deployed the intended change' from 'deployed leftover manifests from a prior environment' until the user notices the cluster is running the wrong thing.

Manually deleting an ApplicationSet-generated child Application (T-28511) produces a Deleting/Syncing flip-flop loop with no in-UI path forward or back. The only known fix is the operational rule captured in notes/note-2.md — switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand — but that step exists only as an incident-review note, not as UI guidance, a blocking confirmation, or an error message at the point the user clicks Delete on a reverse-ordered ApplicationSet's child.

T-27949 (ApplicationSet RollingSync) and T-27875 (auto-sync after #25151's revert) independently produce the same undesigned interface state: Argo CD reports a healthy/synced status (child applicationStatus stuck at Healthy in one case, OutOfSync with no new sync operation queued in the other) while the actual desired spec or revision has diverged from what was applied. In both, the screen shows a clean/green status with no error, warning, or 'sync needed' affordance — the user has no way forward except to already know to cross-check operationState or comparedTo fields by hand.
